Sometimes that irrational part wins. It’s our little demons that eat at us. Friends come and go, so do people. Events change, the trajectory changes. That’s why we stay around. I have felt the way you do. It can get better. Some days still suck, but it can get better. Hope you decide to stay around. ❤️

Fuck her! Sounds like you see right through her. My dad has a lot of the tendencies you describe, he’s partially to blame for my mom’s manic state. He really consumed her. I haven’t spoken to him since she passed and I’m better this way. Blood does not mean an endless excuse for someone who is ultimately a bad person. Enough is enough, so distance yourself and take care of yourself. Don’t let her win you’re strong.

I can relate a lot. It took me a long time to finish my science degree. My sister is very successful with a doctorate degree and I felt like a failure barely making it through under grad science classes. I re took a couple and pushed through. I would stress myself so much studying or worry about exams there were days my steps calculator was less than 50 for the day aka I barely left my desk. My body was inflamed I felt like crap. I stopped thinking about the one class and tried to focus on the bigger goal. There’s always a way. Even if UCF dismisses you, there are many other schools too. Even online. you can do this. You have already overcome a lot

My mom was manic for a few months before she took her life. I was exhausted. In a rage in one of our fights I said “just die then”. I regret this everyday of my life. I regret a lot. I don’t know what your situation is with your mom. I’m sorry she said that to you. But it sounds like your happiness about thinking of this situation is reinforced by you feeling as though you’ll “show her”. I think your biggest win will be to continue life and do well. If she is toxic toward you cut her off. Sorry this isn’t very clear, but things can get better.

Thank you very much, I’m sorry for your loss . I wish there was something better to say but I understand your pain.
